headline.purpose: Not used anywhere in this app -- every screen, including login, is Operate-mode. Title is the ceiling.

title.purpose: This app's workhorse heading -- the top of every list/detail/settings screen.

label.purpose: Form labels, buttons, table headers -- the most-used size given how table-heavy this app is.

caption.purpose: Helper text, status-badge labels, timestamps, audit-log metadata.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for AppCard or the primary button at rest.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover/emphasis elevation, floating overlays (AppSelect dropdown, JalaliDatePicker panel).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Highest-elevation surface -- confirmation modals for destructive/money-moving actions.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Not yet a shared component in this app -- same structural gap provider-panel had before this session's fix.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-accent); color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: none; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); transition: all 150ms; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-strong); box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); }

components.name: Pagination
components.description: Signature component of this app, already implemented well (Pagination.vue) -- an extracted, reusable pagination control neither user-app nor provider-panel has (both still hand-roll per-page). Candidate to back-port, not to fix here.
components.css: .ds-pagination { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; }

narrative.northStar: The Verified Ledger (inherited from apps/user-app -- see apps/provider-panel/DESIGN.md for the sibling reconciliation this app mirrors)
narrative.overview: The operator console for a small internal trust-and-safety/money-moving team. Desktop-primary, table-dense, no Persuade-mode screens at all. Every action here is either money-moving or trust/moderation, both audit-logged, both held to the same elevated confirm-before-commit bar -- the design's job is to make consequence unambiguous, not to be inviting.
keyCharacteristics: Same two-mode teal/violet re-theme as user-app and provider-panel.
The densest, most table-heavy surface in the platform -- desktop information density outranks mobile-friendliness by explicit product mandate.
Two genuinely good existing components (JalaliDatePicker, Pagination) neither sibling app has -- preserve, don't rebuild.
The token layer was found in the same unreconciled state provider-panel was in before this session's fix -- same root cause, same mechanical fix applies.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: On a table-heavy screen, the accent marks exactly the one primary toolbar/header action -- row-level actions are secondary/ghost/danger, never accent-filled.

rules.name: The Uniform Consequence Rule
rules.body: A destructive/trust action and a money-moving action get the same confirm-before-commit treatment and visual weight -- neither category reads as more casual than the other.

rules.name: The Fill-Text Split Rule
rules.body: A fill-safe accent/danger shade is not automatically text-safe -- measure and tokenize both directions separately.

rules.name: The Density-First Rule
rules.body: The strongest form of this rule across all three apps -- no Persuade-mode exception exists here at all.

rules.name: The Elevation-Means-Something Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never decorative -- flat + bordered is the default resting state.

rules.name: The Hue-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never neutral black, even in dark mode.

dos: Do treat apps/user-app/DESIGN.md as the parent and apps/provider-panel/DESIGN.md as the proven sibling fix to mirror.
Do build a shared AppButton/AppInput and migrate hand-rolled markup onto them.
Do apply the same confirm-before-commit weight to money-moving and moderation actions alike.
Do preserve JalaliDatePicker.vue and Pagination.vue as-is.
Do favor table density over mobile-first card layouts.
donts: Don't invent a fourth status-tone vocabulary -- reuse provider-panel's warning/info additions.
Don't soften a destructive or money-moving action's visual weight relative to the other category.
Don't add a mobile-first layout pass at the expense of desktop table density.
